title: Legacy: Why ideas that outlive your name matter more than fame
summary: Jason Cohen argues that the best legacy is the ongoing impact of ideas, not name attribution. Using his own SLC concept being repeated and even plagiarized, he reframes ripples of repetition as the goal, and urges creators to focus on ideas worth repeating over personal attention.

principles.text: Aim for ideas worth repeating, not content that merely drives eyeballs to you.
principles.quote: It means we should worry less about "content" for the sake of "eyeballs" and more about creating ideas that are worth repeating

principles.text: Ideas spread like water waves, independent of their originator; growth comes from repetition and from inspiring remixes.
principles.quote: Waves fizzle out without support, but they grow if whipped up by winds of repetition, and they grow when they inspire other creators, remixing additional ideas into new stones.

principles.text: Treat others repeating or even copying your idea as proof of impact, and meet it with gratitude rather than bitterness.
principles.quote: If the ripples are the legacy, then they can be met instead with gratitude and pride.

principles.text: Make ideas important, true and compelling enough that people want to repeat them even without your name attached.
principles.quote: ideas that are so important and true and compelling and repeatable that people *wish* to repeat them, even if our names aren't attached to the broadcast

principles.text: Focus on positively influencing others and helping them become better versions of themselves rather than on attention to yourself.
principles.quote: We should worry less about the attention we bring to ourselves, and more about how we can positively influence others

principles.text: Attribution and money still matter: artists should be paid, and plagiarism is theft. Ask 'and what else?' beyond fame and money.
principles.quote: Of course attribution is not without value. Artists should be paid for their work.
